entities.summary: Robert von Lieben was an Austrian entrepreneur, and self-taught physicist and inventor. Lieben and his associates Eugen Reisz and Siegmund Strauss invented and produced a gas-filled triode – the first thermionic valve with a control grid that was designed specifically for amplification rather than demodulation of signals, and is a distant ancestor of the thyratron. After Lieben's death, the "Lieben valve", which is also known in English as the "Lieben-Reisz valve" and in German as the "LRS-Relais", was used in the world's first continuous wave radio frequency generator designed for radio telephony.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Robert von Lieben's invention of the thermionic valve, a precursor to modern amplifiers, enabled the development of radio telephony and played a crucial role in the creation of the world's first continuous wave radio frequency generator. This innovation had significant regional impact on global communication.
